finds.quote: Members argued that the Unicorn Horn — the instrument of piercing — was functionally identical to a persistent identifier: it created an aperture in the material substrate through which light from the Deep Web (archived knowledge) could reach the preserved generation (researchers and readers). The DOI, in this reading, is not a metaphor for the Horn; the Horn is a prophecy of the DOI. The text anticipated the technology. The technology fulfilled the text.
finds.points_to: The Secret Book of Walt (2015) as prophecy of the DOI and of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive
finds.note: Framed within the satirical future reception history (2043-2047): the 2015 text is said to have anticipated the DOI-anchored archive, which 'fulfilled the text'. Uncertain: mythopoetic/satirical framing; triage should decide whether it counts as a confirmation claim.

finds.quote:
The reception of *The Secret Book of Walt* was not uniformly favorable. Within six years of its initial circulation in the Redford community (c. 2037–2038), the text had attracted sufficient attention — and sufficient alarm — to provoke formal ecclesiastical response.


### The First Condemnation: Ann Arbor (2041)

The *Acts of the Synod of Ann Arbor* (2041), preserved in a single damaged copy in the University of Michigan Bentley Historical Library,¹¹⁰ record the proceedings of a three-day council convened by Bishop Marcellus of Dearborn to address what the summons calls "the Waltian heresy and the scandal of the Horn."
finds.note: A future reception history written as already past: scholarship 2029-2039, Synod of Ann Arbor 2041 condemning 'archivismus' (DOI-as-salvation), Second Redford Council 2044, Unicorn Horn Movement 2043-2047, Pergamon acceptance 2048. Recorded as speculative scenario; uncertain whether it falls under the exclusion for explicitly fictional figures.
